notes.1-2: 'It struck her that he was lying' = it dawned on her, and a reader can defend 'she concluded' because the gloss 'concluded' reads as reaching a conclusion as well as settling a deal (the 'struck a deal' sense)

notes.0-1: 'The inspector raised a red flag': literally hoisted a flag, or the idiom for voicing (mentioning) a concern
notes.0-2: 'The horse raised its head' = hoisted, and also 'reared its head' (rear = lift up), apart from the bring-up-children sense
notes.0-3: 'raised the bar': physically hoisted the crossbar, or increased the standard; likewise 'raised the water level'
notes.1-3: 'The report raised concerns': brought concerns up (mentioned), or heightened them (increased)
notes.3-4: 'The city raised revenue': collected revenue, or increased it

notes.0-1: 'The series ran for six weeks': was published for six weeks, or extended over six weeks
notes.0-2: 'She ran the newsletter': operated it, or published it; the editor who 'ran the column' can be read either way
notes.0-3: 'The site ran the documentary': published it, or streamed (broadcast) it
notes.1-2: 'The bus line ran from the station to the harbor': the route extended there, or the service operated there
notes.1-3: 'The river ran through the valley': extended through it, or streamed (flowed) through it
notes.1-4: 'The report ran to 300 pages': extended to, or amounted to, 300 pages
notes.2-3: 'The tap ran all night': the tap operated, or water streamed from it; also 'ran the video' = operated/played vs streamed
